- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75% above recent mean), model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast at +5% above peak for next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per day until sentiment stabilizes.  
- Model consistently underestimates in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile (±0.35+ in 3 consecutive days); add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 7–14 days.  
- If recent history shows mean reversion (price drops 5%+ from 10-day high), model often ignores it; forecast should align with 10-day moving average for next 5 days.
